newsitem.title: USA: Barshefsky seeks approval of US ag ambassador.
newsitem.headline: Barshefsky seeks approval of US ag ambassador.

text.p: U.S. Trade Representative Charlene Barshefsky said Thursday she hoped Peter Scher will be approved as the first U.S. Trade Representative ambassador of agriculture within the next six months.

Barshefsky, after speaking to the Emerging Issues forum sponsored by North Carolina State University, said Scher, who was Mickey Kantor's chief of staff at the U.S. Trade Representative's Office and Commerce Department, was "extraordinarily smart and a bulldog."
Scher will have to be approved by the Senate.
"Right now we don't have any one ambassadoral person who focuses solely on agriculture," she said.
Barshefsky said ambassadoral rank would put Scher in position to meet with ministers of foreign countries to discuss agricultural issues at the highest level.
"The idea is to have someone at the rank of a minister, which is what this will do," she said. She and Agriculture Secretary Dan Glickman have worked on this idea for some time, she said.

"This will allow us to field a team between the USDA and USTR at a very high level," she said. "The need is so obvious, I had been a deputy and I know how much time I was able to spend on agricultural issues, and it wasn't nearly enough."

Barshefsky said there is a very strong consensus in Congress that this is the right thing to do and the time is now. Farmers have expressed concern that USTR was not focusing enough attention on agricultural issues and enforcing farm trade agreements.
She said Scher, who was a longtime aide to Sen. Max Baucus, a Montana Democrat, knows grains, cattle, sugar and other commodities.
"We have a very strong ag shop in terms of expertise and will have two more people to come over from USDA to help us out," she said.
